Build OS — The Book

Ten chapters.
Sixty‑five tools.
One method.

Written for the owner who still knows where the shovels are. It takes a company from the day the doors open to the day the business no longer needs you.

The Five A’s
  • 1 Awareness Gathering — get the truth on the table
  • 2 Analyze — sort what matters from what is noise
  • 3 Alignment — put it on a timeline everyone can see
  • 4 Action — one owner, one date, one definition of done
  • 5 Accountability — keep score in the open

Where are you standing?

Every business is somewhere on one journey.

The Snapshot places you honestly. There is no shame in the placement. A Startup is not a failed Scale up, any more than a seed is a failed tree.

1

Startup

The owner does everything, and for now that is correct. Prove that strangers will pay a fair price for what you do, again and again.

Graduates whenDemand is steady, your price holds, and the biggest thing slowing the company down is you.

2

Grow up

The business gets organized. First hires land, cash finds a floor, and the machine gets built piece by piece.

Graduates whenYour best crew lead could run daily operations for two weeks without calling you.

3

Scale up

A leadership team runs the company and you lead the leaders. The goal gets big enough that the old way obviously cannot reach it.

Graduates whenThe company grows while you take real time away, and nobody has to cover for you.

4

Sell off

The owner is optional and the exit is a choice, not a rescue. Sell it, keep it as an asset that pays you, or hand it down.

All three are winsThe trap was never the business. The trap was having no choice.

The Rhythm

Working ON the business only happens
if it is on the calendar first.

Most owners spend all their time working IN it and wonder why nothing changes. Nothing changes because nobody is changing it.

Annual

Retreat to Advance

Two days

The full Five A’s at depth. Dump the season, reset the future page, set four quarters of priorities.

Quarterly

Reset Day

One day

Re-take the Snapshot. Close out and reset the ninety-day priorities. Re-check the seats.

Monthly

Leadership Session

Two hours

Field reports, re-read the future, attack the obstacles in the field, assign owners, confirm the board.

Weekly

Stand-up

Thirty minutes

Numbers on or off track, priority check, clear what is stuck, who does what by when.

Find a Room

Bring your value to the room.
Carry value away.

Business owners carry it alone. Not with a spouse, not with an employee, not with a vendor. A BUILD room is a table of people who have been there, where you get to be seen, heard, and understood, with a little friendly competition on the side.

For Aspiring Facilitators

A great business
doesn’t just happen.
You build it.

You have led teams and made the hard calls. Now you want a room of your own. Put BUILD in front of a table in your city, run it on material that already works, and keep every relationship you make there.

We are not trying to become big and unmanageable. We are trying to be in as many rooms as possible, blessing as many business people as possible, and giving value back to the people who bring their value to the room.

Step OneSupport the networks that already exist. Trade groups, chambers, verticals. Collaboration, not competition.
Step TwoCollaborate to facilitate. You run the room, you connect with the people, and the whole BUILD community comes with you.
Step ThreeCarry the brand. Training through cohorts, the full toolbox, and chapters that carry the BUILD name and DNA.
Start a conversation

Let’s BUILD.
